items.note: Below the yellow band, the raised form card opens with 'Fix 5 fields to continue.' Each field has a red border and its own message with an icon, and the empty name field shows the pink halo focus. The pink 'Create account' lift is the only pink action; the header's 'Sign up' is ink.

Dark version of the same screen: the yellow band keeps its ink text, and the form card sits raised on the black ground. Red field borders and the icon-plus-word messages stay readable, and the focused field's pink halo shows clearly.

On phone the band collapses to title and lead, and the trial list stacks above the one-column form. Every error message sits under its field, the Show button stays next to the password field, and the pink submit stays in the flow.

The form becomes an outlined raised card headed 'Check your inbox' with a pink check, a sentence naming the address the link went to, and one pink 'Back to the home page' lift. It's clear what happened and what to do next.
The confirmation card is a raised dark-grey card with a light border on black. The pink check and the pink return button stay the only accents, and the bolded email address is readable.
The confirmation card stacks under the trial list at full width. Its heading, sentence and pink return button wrap cleanly, and nothing overlaps.

In the periwinkle band, the Yearly pill is selected with a raised fill and ink border, and a 'Billed yearly. You save 20%.' line sits under it. Three outlined plan cards show pink price tags with the yearly totals, and only the middle plan's CTA is pink. Below them come the bordered compare table, disclosure rows with a small sticker, and the closing CTA band.

The band keeps ink text, and in dark the selected Yearly pill turns ink. The plan cards are raised grey with pink price tags and a single pink CTA, and the compare table's borders and check marks stay legible on black.

Plan cards stack cleanly with one pink CTA. The compare table keeps its three-column desktop layout, though: the second plan's header is cut mid-word at the right edge, the third column is off-screen, and nothing shows that the table can scroll.

The first FAQ row is open: its question is underlined, the chevron points up, and the answer sits between the 1px ink rules. A small yellow question sticker sits beside the 'Common questions' heading, as the FAQ row of the 'Applying the concept' table asks.
The FAQ sits on a slightly raised dark section. The open row's answer text and the rules between rows read clearly, and the closed rows keep their chevrons.

Near the bottom of the long phone page, the first question is expanded with its answer between the rules, and the other four stay closed. The hero stickers here sit static below the hero text and stay clear of it.

The teal band for this section holds an ink-filled current-page pill in the header nav. In the 'Customer stories' strip the Education pill is selected (raised fill, ink border). 'Showing 2 of 8 customers' says the result is filtered, and two outlined story cards remain.
Same filtered view in dark: the teal band keeps its ink text, the selected filter pill gets a light border, and the two raised story cards and the result count stay readable.
On phone the filter pills scroll sideways in a strip, cut off after Logistics. Education is selected, the count line is shown, and the two story cards stack at full width under the quote card.

In the footer signup, the email field holding 'nope' has a red border, and an icon-plus-message line under it gives the expected address format. The rest of the long landing page (sticker hero, yellow how-it-works band, ink stat strip) is unchanged and nothing overlaps.
In dark, the footer field's red border and its error line with icon stay readable on the dark footer, and the paper-filled Subscribe button keeps its contrast.

The phone page has the same structure as the desktop page, with the newsletter field and its inline error at the very bottom in the footer. The hero, the stacked feature cards and the yellow band above it stay intact.
Focus sits on the 'Features' nav link: a visible ink outline around the pill, offset from it. It's clearly not the browser default, and nothing else on the page changes.
In dark the focus outline on the 'Features' pill turns pink and stands out on the black header. Every other control stays at rest.
On phone, focus lands on the ink 'Sign up' header button as a clear outline offset from its border. 'Sign up' and the Menu button keep a full-size hit area.

The hero is a flat calendar sticker scene: a periwinkle header, pink, yellow and teal slots, a pointer and a pink check coin with an extruded yellow rim. Four tilted shapes are cropped by the edge (coin, ticket, star, half-disc), all in band colours with heavy ink outlines. Each of the six feature cards gets a different small sticker. They are as clean as the reference's sticker coins.
One small pink coin with an ink rim and a heavy plus glyph sits beside the billing-questions heading. It reads as a coin at its size and follows the coin recipe.
One small pink speech-bubble sticker with an ink outline and three dots tops the quote card. It's a fitting single sticker for a dense section and reads clearly at its size.

Frame strip m1 shows the edge-cropped hero coin with no time-based movement, which fits the spec's scroll-bound drift. Strip m2 shows the trust-pill tag wall moving left at a steady linear pace with the list repeated. Nothing bounces, scales or fades in.

findings.summary: At phone width the plan-comparison table keeps its desktop column layout inside its bordered box. The second plan's column header is cut mid-word at the right edge, the third plan's column is not visible, and nothing shows the table can scroll, so a third of the comparison is hidden. The spec says that under breakpoint.md a table reflows to stacked row blocks.
findings.promptFix: Every table, including comparison or feature matrices on marketing pages, must show all of its columns at 390px. Under breakpoint.md, either reflow it to one stacked block per row (each value labelled with its column name) or, for a comparison of options, one block per option. Never leave columns clipped by the box edge or hidden behind a scroll with no visible cue. Check at 390px that every column header and every value is visible.
